title: Interleaved Phase-Resilient Scheduler for Prefill/Decode
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our current prefill/decode scheduler exhibits tail-latency spikes for mixed tenant workloads with heterogeneous request characteristics (short prompts + long completions, streaming vs non-streaming). Existing phase-splitting strategies either (a) split aggressively and cause kernel thrashing and poor cache locality, or (b) merge phases for throughput but penalize latency-sensitive tenants. This ticket proposes a new Interleaved Phase-Resilient Scheduler (IPRS) that decouples phase granularity from tenant fairness decisions, uses a rentrancy-aware interleaving primitive, and surfaces kernel-selection hints to reduce attention kernel churn and KV-cache fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for latency-sensitive tenant class decreases by >= 20% on mixed workload replay compared to baseline
Overall throughput (tokens/s) drops by <= 5% in same replay compared to baseline
No increase in kernel context-switch rate > 15% (measured by kernel-selection churn metric)
New scheduler integrates with kernel-hint API and can emit hints per-phase with no functional regressions
E2E tests for tenant isolation and eviction scenarios added and passing in CI
decisions: (1) Use interleaved micro-phase windows (default 10 token micro-windows) so short requests can finish in-flight without forcing full phase merges. (2) Expose per-phase kernel_hint (dense_attn | sparse_attn | fused_qkv) to kernel selection layer; kernel selection remains advisory and runtime may override when capacity dictated. (3) Fairness is enforced via a dual-token-credit system: latency-credit and throughput-credit. Latency-sensitive tenants accrue latency-credit that gives micro-windows preferential scheduling up to a soft cap to avoid starvation of throughput tenants.
implementation_notes:
- Add IPRS controller that maintains per-tenant credit buckets and micro-window queues; controller runs in scheduler thread pool.
- Integrate kernel_hint field into Phase proto and propagate through admission -> allocator -> kernel-selector.
- Update KV-cache allocator to prefer colocated micro-windows for same model/version to improve cache hits.
- Add metric kernel_churn_rate and phase_coalescence_ratio.
- Provide runtime flag runtime.scheduler.iprs_enabled and per-tenant override via policy DSL.
test_plan:
- Offline replay: run mixed workload replay (mix from tenant-replays/matrix-2026) comparing baseline scheduler vs IPRS across 3 machines. Measure P50/P95/P99, throughput, kernel churn.
- Unit tests for credit accounting and eviction logic.
- Integration test that simulates kernel-selection overrides and verifies no deadlocks.
- Chaos test: kill a kernel-worker mid-micro-window and assert graceful reschedule/fallback path works and metrics reflect hedging.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated rollout to alpha cluster (runtime-1.21-canary) for 1 week on small traffic. 2) Observe P95 and kernel_churn for regressions. 3) Gradual rollout to dedicated clusters with A/B (10% -> 50% -> 100%) if metrics stable for 72h. 4) Default enabled for new tenants after 2 weeks of stable telemetry. 5) Provide opt-out per-tenant for 4 weeks post rollout.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: aggressive micro-windowing could increase kernel context switches and reduce throughput. Mitigation: backoff mechanism that merges consecutive micro-windows into larger phases if kernel_churn_rate crosses threshold.
Risk: kernel_hint mismatch may cause suboptimal kernel selection. Mitigation: conservative default mapping and runtime percentile-based override + telemetry to refine mapping.
Risk: unfair starvation of throughput tenants if latency-credit abused. Mitigation: hard token cap and sliding-window decay on latency-credit accrual.
